tasks.short: Approve the standard message for results already marked normal, let those patients know, phone patients with abnormal results, and explain procedures and discuss test results or prescribed treatments with patients in consultations.

steps.what: General practitioner approves the practice's standard message for a patient whose results they marked normal
General practitioner lets patients with normal test results know
General practitioner phones patients to discuss abnormal test results
General practitioner explains procedures and discusses test results or prescribed treatments with patients in consultations

tasks.design: Reviewing and marking results belongs to the task on interpreting tests, and the consultation note to the task on keeping patient records; their savings are counted there, not here. Once the GP has marked a result normal, they approve the practice's standard message for that patient and the portal sends it instead of a phone call; patients without the portal are still phoned. Abnormal results are phoned, and explaining and discussing results and treatments stay with the GP.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals that carry result messages with standard texts.
tasks.still_hard: Some patients want to hear even a normal result from their GP.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a frightening result so the patient can still sleep.

reach.learn: Whether result calls to the practice fall.

evidence.claim: Patient portals can send result messages with a standard text after the doctor marks the result.

assumptions: Boundary: telling patients about results and discussing them; reviewing results and writing the note are sibling tasks and carry no savings here.
Input contract for s1: results marked normal by the GP in the record as part of interpreting tests; standard texts approved by the practice.
About 70% of patients use the portal; the rest are phoned; s2 is priced at that share.
Patients read the portal message in about the time a call took; no added patient time.
Discussing results and treatments does not change.
unknowns: Share of patients using the portal.
research_questions: Do patients phone back about portal results?

incremental.description: General practitioner keeps the standard result texts current with the practice.

approvals.approved_version: The standard normal-result message for this patient and these results, as approved by the GP in s1; a new result needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients on the portal; high: 70% of patients on the portal.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise patients on diet, activity, hygiene and prevention in consultations, choose patient information, give it to the patient, answer e-consult questions, and give talks to community groups.

steps.what: General practitioner advises patients concerning diet, activity, hygiene and disease prevention
General practitioner chooses patient information leaflets for the patient
General practitioner gives the patient the chosen leaflets; after the choice in s2 the record sends them as links to the patient's portal
Patients send e-consult questions about lifestyle and prevention
General practitioner answers e-consult questions
General practitioner gives talks on prevention to community groups

tasks.design: The record ({OTHER}) offers a pick list of vetted, guideline-based patient information pages per topic; the GP chooses the pages, and once chosen the links go to the patient in the portal instead of printed leaflets. The practice website points patients to the same pages before they send an e-consult, and the GP links pages in replies. Advising in consultations and community talks stay with the GP; no generated advice is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were found and printed in the consultation, and e-consult answers written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Guideline-based patient information sites cover most lifestyle and prevention topics.
tasks.still_hard: Advice works only when it fits the patient's life.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the one change a patient is ready to make.

reach.learn: Whether patients read the pages they were sent.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts gives guideline-based patient information, made by the NHG with the FMS and the Patiëntenfederatie.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient's concern to the talk given; treatment is outside.
Input contract: vetted information pages from the national site; fallback is printed leaflets.
Patients read the vetted pages on the website before sending a question; priced as customer time.
Advising and talks do not change.
research_questions: Do e-consult questions on lifestyle fall?

incremental.description: General practitioner checks the pick list after guideline updates.
Patients read vetted information pages before sending a question.

approvals.approved_version: The links to the information pages chosen by the GP in s2, sent to that patient's portal; a different patient or page needs a new choice.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older patients who prefer printed leaflets; high: most patients use the portal and website.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold the daily practice huddle, supervise assistants' triage, supervise GP trainees and students, check delegated tasks, and plan who covers which tasks.

steps.what: General practitioner holds the daily practice huddle with nurses and assistants
General practitioner directs assistants' triage and answers their questions
General practitioner supervises GP trainees and medical students
General practitioner checks tasks delegated to nurses and assistants
General practitioner plans who covers which tasks in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Tasks delegated to nurses and assistants under practice protocols show in a task list in the record ({OTHER}), with status and anything that needs the GP's eye, so the GP checks exceptions instead of each task. Cover for tasks is planned in the practice's scheduling tool ({HCM}) with skills per staff member. The huddle, directing triage and supervising trainees stay with the GP; the task list is not used to rate staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delegated tasks were checked case by case and cover planned in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice records offer task lists per protocol; scheduling tools hold skills.
tasks.still_hard: Triage questions come in all day and need an answer at once.
tasks.human_edge: Backing an assistant who made a hard triage call.

reach.learn: Whether questions to the GP fall.

evidence.claim: Practice records can show task lists for delegated protocol work with status per patient.
Systems that can monitor staff performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the day schedule to the task cover plan; hiring staff is outside.
Input contract: protocols set by the practice; skills kept in the scheduling tool; fallback is case-by-case checks and spreadsheets.
The huddle, triage directions and supervising trainees do not change.
research_questions: Are delegated tasks completed on time more often?

incremental.description: General practitioner keeps protocol task rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small practice with few delegated tasks; high: a large practice with many protocols.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Join multidisciplinary meetings, consult pharmacists and other providers, write referral letters, send referrals, and read letters and reports from other providers.

steps.what: General practitioner coordinates care with nurses, social workers and psychologists in multidisciplinary meetings
General practitioner phones pharmacists and other providers about patients
General practitioner writes referral letters

loop.input: The GP's reason for referral, the problem list, medication and relevant results from the record.
loop.output: A draft referral letter in the receiver's format.
loop.check: Medication and results in the letter come from the record by code, not the model; the GP reads, edits and signs every letter.
loop.stop: No letter leaves unsigned; after one failed redraft the GP writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: The reason for referral and history need prose; a template fills only the structured fields.

steps.what: General practitioner sends the referral to the receiving provider
General practitioner reads letters and reports from other providers

tasks.design: Secure messaging with pharmacists and other providers in the regional care network carries the patient's context, so fewer phone calls are needed. A certified tool drafts referral letters from the GP's reason for referral and the record; medication and results come from the record by code, and once the GP has signed, the referral goes through the referral system. Structured reports from other providers file into the record with the key changes on top. Multidisciplinary meetings stay with the GP.
tasks.previous_blocker: Providers were reached by phone, and letters written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified tools draft referral letters; regional networks offer secure messaging.
tasks.still_hard: Complex patients need a real conversation between providers.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing with a psychologist who leads the care for a shared patient.
tasks.altitude: The GP edits and signs letters instead of writing them.

evidence.claim: Juvoly drafts referral letters and suggests ICPC, ICD-10 and SNOMED codes; Tandem's scribe and coding carry MDR class IIa.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI: know whether it is a medical device, assess risks, train, test and monitor.

assumptions: Boundary: from shared patients to processed reports; the other providers' care is outside.
Input contract: record data by integration; receivers' formats from the referral system; fallback is phone and writing by hand.
Other providers' time is outside the GP's savings.
research_questions: How much of a drafted letter does the GP change?

already_counted.description: General practitioner edits and signs drafted letters.

incremental.description: General practitioner reports wrong drafts to the practice's AI contact.

approvals.approved_version: The referral letter as edited and signed by the GP in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few referrals and providers outside the network; high: many referrals and most providers on secure messaging.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The general practitioner keeps explaining, advising, directing staff and agreeing care with others; result calls, typed notes, printed leaflets and blank-page letters shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A GP with longer consultations for patients who need them.
